name: Kerbrute - Enumerate AD Usernames
description: Validates which usernames exist in Active Directory by abusing Kerberos pre-authentication responses, without causing failed logons or lockouts. Confirmed users become targets for spraying or AS-REP roasting.

examples.label: Enumerate valid AD usernames via Kerberos

notes:
kerbrute abuses Kerberos pre-auth to enumerate valid AD usernames WITHOUT logging failures (no 4625). Feed a name list; valid users come back fast. Prereq for AS-REP roasting and spraying.
Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 19 (Password Attacks)

recommended.note: Build the candidate username list first.
Password spraying tries one password against many accounts to stay under lockout thresholds, optionally across a whole subnet.
Online password brute force against a network service.

defense.why_it_works: Kerbrute enumerates valid AD usernames by sending AS-REQs and reading the KDC's response (valid vs unknown user) - and can spray - without generating 4625.
defense.prerequisites: Network access to a DC (Kerberos 88) and a username list.
defense.impact: A validated list of domain usernames (and, when spraying, valid credentials).
defense.detection: Failed authentication bursts: Windows 4625 (failed logon) and 4771 (Kerberos pre-auth failed) at abnormal rate/volume; account lockouts (4740); many attempts from one source, or - for spraying - one password across many accounts. SIEM correlation on failed-logon spikes.
defense.artifacts: Kerberos 4768 pre-auth requests for many usernames; unknown users return distinct errors - a user-enumeration pattern.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4768 Result_Code=0x6
| stats dc(Account_Name) as accts by Client_Address, bin(_time, 1m)
| where accts>25
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4768 and Status == "0x6"
| summarize accts=dcount(TargetUserName) by IpAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where accts > 25
| sort by accts desc
// KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN burst = username enumeration
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1110 M1032 Multi-factor Authentication] MFA defeats password guessing; [M1027 Password Policies] strong passwords + [M1036 Account Use Policies] lockout thresholds; alert on failed-logon spikes and impossible-travel.
defense.evasion: Enumeration via AS-REQ avoids 4625 failed-logon events (quieter than LDAP/SMB brute); spray slowly to avoid 4771 spikes.
defense.misconfiguration: Password policies are insufficiently strict: minimum length too short (< 12 chars), no complexity requirement, no history check (allows password reuse), no lockout or too-lenient lockout threshold. Combined with credential reuse across services, a single cracked hash grants access to multiple systems.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Weak domain password policy:
Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy
# MinPasswordLength:    8    <-- too short
# PasswordHistoryCount: 0    <-- no history, password reuse allowed
# ComplexityEnabled:    False <-- no complexity
# LockoutThreshold:     0    <-- NO lockout

# Local SAM policy (workgroup machines):
# Control Panel -> Local Security Policy -> Account Policies -> Password Policy
# Same weak defaults as above
defense.secure_config:
# Set a strong domain password policy:
Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -Identity corp.local \
    -MinPasswordLength 14 \
    -PasswordHistoryCount 24 \
    -ComplexityEnabled $true \
    -MaxPasswordAge 90.00:00:00 \
    -LockoutThreshold 5 \
    -LockoutDuration 00:30:00 \
    -LockoutObservationWindow 00:30:00

# Fine-Grained PSO for privileged accounts (stricter):
New-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Name PrivilegedPSO \
    -MinPasswordLength 20 -PasswordHistoryCount 48 \
    -ComplexityEnabled $true -LockoutThreshold 3 \
    -LockoutDuration 01:00:00 -Precedence 1
Add-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicySubject PrivilegedPSO -Subjects 'Domain Admins'

# Deploy Azure AD Password Protection (blocks common passwords on-prem too)
# Enable Microsoft Entra ID Smart Lockout

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

variations.label: Password spray
variations.description: Performs password spraying via Kerberos pre-authentication using Kerbrute. Tests a single password against many accounts - generates fewer alerts than NTLM-based spraying.

variations.label: Brute-force one user
variations.description: Brute-forces passwords for a single user via Kerberos pre-authentication. Tests multiple passwords against one account using Kerbrute.

explain:
Validates which usernames exist in AD via Kerberos pre-auth, without lockouts:
  kerbrute userenum        enumerate valid users from KDC responses
  --dc <dc_ip>             the Domain Controller
  --domain <domain>        the domain
  <names_file>             candidate usernames
Valid users give a distinct response and no failed-logon events; confirmed accounts become spray/AS-REP-roast targets. bruteuser brute-forces one user's password instead.
